name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills, known as the Scotland of the East. Colonial hill station with pleasant climate, markets, churches, parks and gateway to the Khasi Hills attractions.
facts: State capital and East Khasi Hills HQ
Base for exploring Sohra and surrounding attractions

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest point in Meghalaya at about 1,965 m, offering panoramic views of Shillong city, surrounding hills and plains of Bangladesh on clear days. Sacred to the Khasi as the abode of U Lei Shillong.
facts: Sacred sanctum of U Lei Shillong
Popular for sunset views and photography

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tiered waterfall in Upper Shillong, named after a rock formation resembling an elephant. Easily accessible with pathways, surrounded by lush greenery; one of the most popular short excursions from the city.
facts: Local name Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew

name: Ward's Lake
description: Artificial horseshoe-shaped lake in the heart of Shillong, named after Sir William Ward. Features gardens, a wooden bridge, boating and is a popular leisure spot for locals and visitors.
facts: Man-made lake also known as Pollock Lake or Nan Polok

name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures
description: Major museum in Mawlai, Shillong, showcasing the cultures, traditions, lifestyles and artefacts of indigenous peoples of Northeast India across multiple galleries.
facts: Also known as Don Bosco Museum

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Historic town in East Khasi Hills, formerly one of the wettest places on Earth. Gateway to dramatic waterfalls, limestone caves, living root bridges and viewpoints overlooking the Bangladesh plains.
facts: Base for Nohkalikai, Mawsmai and root bridges

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India at about 340 m, dropping from the Sohra plateau into a turquoise pool. Dramatic cliff-top viewpoint; especially powerful during and after monsoon.
facts: Tallest single-drop plunge waterfall in India
Legend associated with local woman Likai

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Accessible limestone cave near Sohra with electric lighting, stalactites and stalagmites. Short walk through chambers; popular and family-friendly cave experience in the region.
facts: Near Mawsmai village and Seven Sisters Falls
Local name Krem Mawsmai (Oath Stone Cave)

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters Falls)
description: Series of seven parallel waterfalls cascading down limestone cliffs near Mawsmai, offering panoramic views towards the Bangladesh plains. Best during monsoon when all segments are visible.

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Iconic two-tier living root bridge grown from Ficus elastica roots by Khasi communities over generations in Nongriat village. Requires a steep trek of about 3,500 steps from Tyrna; unique bio-engineering marvel.
facts: Can be extended to Rainbow Falls

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Widely known as Asia’s cleanest village, with bamboo pathways, flower gardens and a nearby single-tier living root bridge at Riwai. Community-managed eco-tourism destination near the Bangladesh border.
facts: Riwai Living Root Bridge short walk away

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic canyon viewpoint offering sweeping vistas of deep gorges, green hills and valleys. Popular for photography and short visits; access via a short walk from the parking area.

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient sacred grove preserved by Khasi traditional religious sanctions. Rich in biodiversity with unique flora, orchids and butterflies; guided walks available. Part of the David Scott Trail area.
facts: Starting point for David Scott Trail

name: Arwah Cave
description: Limestone cave near Sohra famous for marine fossils (shells and fish bones) visible in the walls. Accessible via a short paved trail with cliff views; less crowded than Mawsmai.
facts: Also known as Krem Arwah or Lumshynna Cave
